## Purpose

Global CSS design tokens for the run subtree. **`globals.css` is the canonical, actively-used
token layer** (imported by [app/layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx)); [theme.ts](../../frontend/src/styles/theme.ts) is an older TypeScript token module that
has zero importers anywhere in the codebase and appears to be dead scaffolding left over from an
earlier design pass.

(No entries in `imports`/`imported_by` above because a plain CSS `import` isn't a TS module edge
the dependency graph tracks — `globals.css` is very much wired in via [app/layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx).)

## Shape

- `globals.css` — Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` token layer, labeled in its own header comment as
  the "Canonical Token Layer (D-15 / SC-1)": one brand chroma (`#3C2CDA`), a warm ink ramp,
  beige/paper surfaces, line/border tokens, and a status color ramp
  (running/done/failed/amber/queued). Font CSS vars (`--font-sans`, `--font-serif`) bind to
  `next/font` vars exposed by [app/layout.tsx](../../frontend/src/app/layout.tsx). Explicitly scoped to "the run subtree" —
  downstream shells (multiple phases, per the header comment) gate on this layer rather than
  forking a per-page palette.
- [theme.ts](../../frontend/src/styles/theme.ts) — a `colors`/`theme` object (navy/white/grey/black "Enterprise-dark" palette) with
  `ThemeColors`/`ThemeAnimation` type exports. Grep confirms nothing imports it.
- [__tests__/token-layer.test.ts](../../frontend/src/styles/__tests__/token-layer.test.ts) — reads `globals.css` off disk (via `fs`/`path`, hence the
  External deps) and asserts on its token contents directly, since there's no TS module to
  import.

## Why this shape

`globals.css` uses Tailwind's `@theme inline` mechanism specifically so the token layer
participates in Tailwind's generated utility classes (`bg-brand`, `text-status-failed`, etc.)
rather than requiring a parallel JS theme object to stay in sync by hand — which is likely
exactly why [theme.ts](../../frontend/src/styles/theme.ts) fell out of use: once the CSS-native token layer existed, a duplicate TS
color object had no consumers left. **It was left in the tree rather than deleted** (this task
does not remove it — only documents it).

The CSS-file test ([token-layer.test.ts](../../frontend/src/styles/__tests__/token-layer.test.ts)) exists because a CSS custom-property layer can't be
unit tested through a normal TS import; reading and asserting on the raw file content is the
only way to guard token names/values with the existing vitest setup.
